slides.title: Practice counts *before it looks good.*
slides.sub: What an Oxford study of new jugglers found in their brain scans.

slides.title: The study
slides.body: 48 adults who couldn't juggle. Half practiced, about 30 minutes a day for six weeks. Everyone had brain scans before and after.

slides.title: What changed
slides.body: The practice group showed changes in white matter, the brain's wiring, in areas used for reaching and grasping.

slides.title: The surprising part
slides.body: The changes showed up in everyone who trained, however well they juggled. The researchers point to time spent practicing, not skill.

slides.title: Count the reps, not the results.
slides.body: Pick one thing you're working on. This week, track how often you practice it, not how well it went.
